To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) deep RL outperforms GP methods on summary state/action spaces, and (2) a two-stage training approach based on a deep RL actor-critic policy network can learn efficiently from a small amount of dialogues.
(1) RL can be used in dialogue systems, and (2) deep RL can be trained efficiently on original state and action space.
(1) Deep policy networks trained with an actor-critic method outperforms Gaussian processes methods for dialogue management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following contributions.
the use of deep policy networks to train dialogue systems with two-stage training.
the use of deep policy networks with two-stage training (supervised + batch RL) for dialogue systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method, which is based on the use of deep neural networks and a two-stage training process, can be successfully used for dialogue system development.
the deep policy networks with two-stage training are a promising approach for dialogue systems.
the proposed method is a very efficient and practical approach to dialogue policy learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how deep RL can be used to learn policies on large state-action spaces, how it can be trained on a small dataset and how it can be bootstrapped from batch RL.
deep RL methods can be trained efficiently on dialogue systems with a small amount of dialogues.
we propose a new method to train dialogue systems that is both data-efficient and converges faster than other methods.

deep policy networks are a promising direction to pursue for dialogue management.
